title: Habits Take About 59 Days, Not 21
safety: General wellness only. The trial studied one everyday nutrition behaviour, so the timing is a reference point rather than a rule for every habit.

beats.headline: Habits took about 59 days, not twenty one
beats.body: In a 2021 trial, the people who did form a habit hit peak automatic feeling after a median of 59 days. The twenty one day rule was never a research finding.

beats.headline: Automatic means you stop deciding
beats.body: Automaticity is the point where a behaviour runs without much thought. The trial tracked it with daily surveys, and it built up slowly rather than switching on.

beats.headline: Pick the cue you will actually repeat
beats.body: A cue is the thing that reminds you to start. Anchoring to a daily routine worked no better than a set clock time, so you could pick whichever one sticks.

beats.headline: Count repetitions, not days
beats.body: Repeating the plan was the strongest predictor in the trial. A good place to start is a simple tally of how many times you have actually done it.

beats.headline: Give it about two months
beats.body: Expect roughly two months before it feels easy, and remember the study followed one everyday nutrition habit. Your own timing may sit either side of that.

beats.headline: Slower is not failing
beats.body: If it still takes effort today, that is just where you are on the path. Nothing has gone wrong. You could simply do it once more tomorrow.
